extracted.intended_audience: audio journalists, podcast producers, public media newsrooms, and grant applicants to the Knight Foundation
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for selecting, producing, and funding journalistic podcasts, emphasizing audio-specific newsworthiness, format and distribution fit, and funder (Knight Foundation) investment priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intimacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice creates personal connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the human voice and conversational delivery to build a close relationship between storyteller and listener; prioritize vocal choices that convey closeness and presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone, pace, and music carry feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage tone of voice, rhythmic pacing, and musical cues to communicate emotional content that might be harder to convey in print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural speech and ambient sound convey authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor unscripted, natural-sounding speech and use ambient/room sounds to make scenes feel real and believable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-shifting
rubrics_metrics.description: Listeners control when they consume the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design episodes and pacing assuming on-demand listening; structure content so it remains effective regardless of when the listener tunes in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility
rubrics_metrics.description: Podcasts are consumed while commuting, exercising, or moving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider listening contexts (noisy, hands-busy) when writing and editing—clarity, pacing, and sound mixing should suit mobile listening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong central character with audible voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects should have a strong, audible presence that works in audio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose subjects whose voices (literal or narrative personality) can carry a story; the subject’s voice should reveal character and propel the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid setting that can be sonically captured
rubrics_metrics.description: Settings should offer ambient or evocative sounds that translate to audio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select stories taking place in sound-rich environments (markets, factories, nature, homes) where ambient audio can create scene and mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear narrative arc
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories need a beginning, middle, and end appropriate to audio storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure episodes (or series) with a discernible narrative arc so listeners understand stakes and resolution; avoid diffuse, unfocused story paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict / tension
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict or tension that drives listener attention is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify clear tensions or stakes that keep audiences engaged and wanting resolution; use pacing and sound to heighten tension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice reveals what print doesn't — emotional honesty matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize moments of vulnerability or candidness in interviews that expose emotional reality and deepen listener empathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise / mystery
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements of surprise or unresolved mystery keep listeners engaged until resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use narrative hooks and withheld information (where ethical) to sustain curiosity across an episode or series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of dialogue and multiple perspectives strengthens audio storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mix interviews, witnesses, experts, and narration to create dynamic audio textures and balance points of view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-rich subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that can be developed over time (episodes/series) fit podcast formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor subjects with evolving elements or layered details that justify episodic treatment or deeper serial reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound quality
rubrics_metrics.description: High-quality recording and audio production are essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in clear recording, good microphones, and postproduction mixing; poor sound quality undermines credibility and listenability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambient sound present where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Using ambient sound to set scene and authenticity is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture location audio to enrich storytelling and provide aural cues about place and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple speakers and vocal textures prevent monotony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include varied voices—hosts, subjects, reporters—to maintain interest and contrast tonalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music as emotional cue
rubrics_metrics.description: Music should be used to signal emotional beats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply music intentionally to support moods and transitions; avoid overuse that distracts from reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Variation in pacing prevents monotony and sustains engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate tempos, use pauses and cuts strategically, and tailor segment lengths to content and attention spans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length appropriate to subject
rubrics_metrics.description: Episode length must fit the complexity and demands of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose concise formats for simple topics and longer episodes/series for in-depth material; do not pad or shorten to fit arbitrary runtimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episodic suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Some stories naturally fit serial/episodic formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a subject benefits from episodic unfolding (e.g., investigations, long-form narratives) rather than single-episode coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binge-worthy
rubrics_metrics.description: Content that encourages continued listening across episodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design series with hooks and coherent throughlines that make listeners want to progress to the next episode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotable
rubrics_metrics.description: Segments that produce shareable clips for social distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include memorable lines or moments that can be clipped for promotion and audience growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Niche-defining
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct subject matter that defines a podcast’s niche.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a clear editorial identity or unique angle that differentiates the podcast in crowded markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-interest content (Knight Foundation investment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content should serve the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize reporting that informs civic life, supports accountability, or serves democratic functions when seeking Knight support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underserved communities (Knight Foundation investment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that reaches or represents underserved audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target coverage and distribution strategies that engage communities lacking robust local/niche media.

rubrics_metrics.name: New voices (Knight Foundation investment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for creators beyond established public radio veterans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund projects that expand who gets to tell stories—diverse producers, independent creators, and nontraditional backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainable models (Knight Foundation investment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should demonstrate potential for financial or operational sustainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show plans for revenue, audience growth, partnerships, or cost structures that suggest longevity beyond one-off grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust-building potential (Knight Foundation investment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Podcasts should help build or restore audience trust in news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design editorial practices, transparency, and engagement strategies that cultivate credibility and long-term relationships with listeners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility (Knight Foundation investment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure content is accessible to diverse audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider transcripts, captioning, distribution on accessible platforms, and inclusive language to lower barriers to access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse perspectives (Knight Foundation investment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include geographic and demographic diversity in voices and viewpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recruit contributors and subjects from varied backgrounds to broaden representation and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre-specific criteria (daily, investigative, explainer, interview, narrative documentary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different podcast genres have distinct evaluation criteria: daily news (timeliness, brevity, host voice); investigative serial (story development, mystery, characters); explainer (simplifying complex topics); interview show (personality, expertise, format); narrative documentary (scene-based audio).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match form to content: for daily shows emphasize speed and concise hosting; for serial investigations emphasize unfolding mystery and character arcs; for explainers focus on clarity and accessible framing; for interviews prioritize host personality and guest selection; for narrative documentaries focus on scene construction and audio dramatization (Wolfe-style scenes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit audio newsworthiness checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Underlying desirable qualities: audible voice of subject; sound-rich environment; personal story potential; long enough for development; universal theme beneath specifics; distinct host voice; listener time investment justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist when vetting ideas—ensure the story has at least several of these properties to justify production resources and listener attention; where items overlap existing criteria (e.g., audible voice, sound-rich environment) prioritize them in assignment and preproduction decisions.
